reason: The text presents the opposite scenario. The Hebrew people are actively and freely expressing their views and making demands. When Moses is delayed on the mountain, the people gather themselves together and vocally petition Aaron ('And they said unto him, Up, make us gods...'). They speak their demands openly without apparent discouragement. The text shows people expressing themselves quite freely, though the expression involves idolatry. The consequences of severe punishment come after they have expressed themselves, not as a prior discouragement preventing speech. There is no evidence in the passage of any mechanism that discourages the people from expressing their views; rather, the passage demonstrates their willingness to voice grievances and demands.
